chunks: And the evil of the darkening night when it overspreads,

key_terms.غَاسِقٍ: The darkening night or the star that darkens

ai.seo_question: What does 'Itha Waqab' mean in the context of seeking refuge from the evil of the night?
ai.summary: This phrase, drawn from Surah Al-Falaq (113:2), invokes protection against the 'darkening night' (Al-Ghasiq) as it spreads its gloom (Itha Waqab), a concept deeply rooted in pre-Islamic and early Islamic cosmology where night was associated with unseen dangers and jinn. In Shia tafsir, scholars like Allamah Tabatabai emphasize this as a plea for divine safeguarding from both physical darkness and spiritual obscurity, highlighting the transition from twilight to full night as a critical time for spiritual vigilance.
